EVIDENCE: Winner median r120 percentile is 0.602302 versus 0.518005 for losers; top-20 median is 0.608925.
Top weighted-RS quartile has a positive 0.1115% median and 5.3973% mean cycle return, versus the V1 aggregate -0.9705% median and 3.0456% mean.
Winner and loser r20 medians are nearly indistinguishable (0.687239 versus 0.694883), so the new evidence is horizon interaction rather than a repeat of the prior no-RS ablation.
hypotheses.EXPECTED_BENEFIT: Suppress entries whose short/mid-horizon strength is not confirmed by persistent cross-sectional strength, improving median trade and return excluding the largest winners without adding a new data source.
hypotheses.EXPECTED_COST: Fewer entries and possible loss of some large winners whose r120 percentile is below the cross-sectional median.
hypotheses.MECHANISM: The existing weighted RS score can admit a security whose short or medium horizon dominates despite below-median persistent relative strength.
hypotheses.OBSERVED_V1_FAILURE: V1 has a negative median cycle return and -50.1573% return excluding the best 20 cycles while retaining positive right-tail winners.
hypotheses.PROPOSED_MINIMAL_CHANGE: Require the already-computed r120 cross-sectional percentile to be at least the semantic median (0.50) at entry; one optional second variant may require all existing r20/r60/r120 percentiles to be at least 0.50.
hypotheses.WHY_V1_MAY_CAUSE_IT: V1 ranks the weighted 20/60/120 score but has no horizon-consistency admission check, allowing strong short-term rank to compensate for weak persistent rank.

EVIDENCE: Twenty-two cycles ending at or below -10% contribute -413236.91 of realized P&L.
The <=-10% band has median MFE +4.1982% and median MAE -14.0699%, unlike the top-20 winners with median MFE +55.2179% and median MAE -1.8924%.
A next-session execution boundary is required; no same-bar exit may be introduced.
hypotheses.EXPECTED_BENEFIT: Cap the severe-loss tail while preserving most right-tail winners.
hypotheses.EXPECTED_COST: Gap-through execution can still exceed the threshold, and a stop can truncate eventual winners; top-20 p10 MAE is -6.1294%, so a tighter threshold is not justified.
hypotheses.MECHANISM: V1 waits for existing trend/set exits after a position has entered a persistent adverse path, permitting a small severe-loss tail to absorb a large part of gross winner P&L.
hypotheses.OBSERVED_V1_FAILURE: The 58 cycles at or below -5% contribute -759848.23, including 22 cycles at or below -10%.
hypotheses.PROPOSED_MINIMAL_CHANGE: If tested, add one close-confirmed -10% cycle-return risk exit, submitted only for the next eligible open under existing execution rules; no tighter sweep.
hypotheses.WHY_V1_MAY_CAUSE_IT: Existing individual and market exits are trend conditions rather than an explicit position loss budget.

EVIDENCE: Thirty-nine cycles with coincident individual-MA and set-removal exit lineage have 25.64% win rate, -6.9250% median return, and -282649.41 realized P&L.
The prior basic individual-exit disable ablation used a different sample and showed a trade-off; simply repeating that ablation is prohibited and scientifically insufficient.
hypotheses.EXPECTED_BENEFIT: Potentially reduce the specific weak-security exit interaction without disturbing market exits that carry most V1 winner P&L.
hypotheses.EXPECTED_COST: The frozen decomposition is descriptive and does not identify a unique causal intervention; changing confirmation may also discard recoveries.
hypotheses.MECHANISM: A security-specific trend break and contemporaneous eligibility removal identify a particularly weak path, but the current evidence does not isolate which exit component causes the loss.
hypotheses.OBSERVED_V1_FAILURE: The combined individual-MA/set-removal lineage is the weakest sizeable exit bucket.
hypotheses.PROPOSED_MINIMAL_CHANGE: None authorized yet; do not disable the individual exit or add an interaction rule without a uniquely falsifiable causal specification.
hypotheses.WHY_V1_MAY_CAUSE_IT: V1 can remain in weak names until two-close confirmation or removal, but the observed bucket alone is not a counterfactual.

EVIDENCE: The 28 entries that fail the existing breakout-volume shadow diagnostic have 53.57% win rate, +0.5169% median return, and +2.9808% mean return.
The 166 shadow-pass entries have 43.98% win rate and -1.2620% median return.
hypotheses.EXPECTED_BENEFIT: None supported by the frozen 2018-2021 evidence.
hypotheses.EXPECTED_COST: A hard gate would remove a small group with better median and win-rate behavior.
hypotheses.MECHANISM: Turn the existing shadow breakout-volume check into an entry requirement.
hypotheses.OBSERVED_V1_FAILURE: Potential low-quality entries were considered as a source of the negative median.
hypotheses.WHY_V1_MAY_CAUSE_IT: The proposed mechanism is contradicted rather than supported by the frozen sample.

EVIDENCE: The maximum run of nonpositive completed cycles is 10 and losses cluster in several exit months.
The decomposition does not establish an ex-ante authorized regime feature that uniquely predicts those clusters.
hypotheses.EXPECTED_BENEFIT: Could reduce repeated exposure during an adverse strategy regime.
hypotheses.EXPECTED_COST: Adds path dependence, a cooldown length, and likely misses rebounds or right-tail entries; it is highly susceptible to fitting the observed cluster chronology.
hypotheses.MECHANISM: Temporarily suppress new entries after a sequence of realized losses.
hypotheses.OBSERVED_V1_FAILURE: Losses are temporally clustered and include a ten-cycle nonpositive streak.
hypotheses.PROPOSED_MINIMAL_CHANGE: No candidate tonight; retain as deferred research unless an independently authorized causal regime trigger is established.
hypotheses.WHY_V1_MAY_CAUSE_IT: V1 has no portfolio-level loss-regime state, but realized-loss timing is itself an outcome and is not enough to justify a tuned cooldown.

EVIDENCE: 2018 is negative despite only 2.8755% average invested ratio and 85.19% flat sessions.
2019-2021 average invested ratio is approximately 30-34%, so high exposure is not a common explanation across years.
hypotheses.EXPECTED_BENEFIT: No standalone exposure change is supported.
hypotheses.EXPECTED_COST: Reducing exposure would likely suppress both losses and the sparse large winners without addressing selection quality.
hypotheses.MECHANISM: Reduce position count or gross exposure to control drawdown.
hypotheses.OBSERVED_V1_FAILURE: V1 has uneven annual results and a -20.7627% maximum drawdown.
hypotheses.PROPOSED_MINIMAL_CHANGE: No change; do not repeat exposure-matched or position-count ablations without a new interaction.
hypotheses.WHY_V1_MAY_CAUSE_IT: The cross-year exposure evidence does not support overexposure as the primary failure.
